name: Question 3
problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=2$ and $y=\frac{x}{2}.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/990f2180e92ffa9ae0b77a7c8c4aae284cacf03f7a7a62b1ed0b56f24705d671.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/db7fe0aa7b746eab86c011545ec37d59d8f225f02a9fc6f4388754e1c528db8c.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,-x\le y\le 2}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\frac{1}{2}x\le y\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-x}^{2}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx+{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{x/2}^{2}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=−x, y=2 and y=x2. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫01∫−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫12∫x/22f(x,y)dydx
b
∫−20∫−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫04∫2x/2f(x,y)dydx
c
∫01∫2−xf(x,y)dydx+∫12∫x/22f(x,y)dydx
d
∫−20∫−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫04∫x/22f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−20∫2−xf(x,y)dydx+∫04∫x/22f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−2≤x≤0,−x≤y≤2}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤x≤4,12x≤y≤2}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−20∫−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫04∫x/22f(x,y)dydx.
